Did I enjoy my time with this game? It was alright. Do I recommend this game? Hell no lol. This game is the ARPG genre boiled down into its simplest form, taking the "number goes up" and gear grind formula from them and turning it into some sort of back alley drug. It is super fun at first seeing all the numbers go up and getting new gear and skills. But eventually you realize all melee weapons feel the same, both ranged weapons end up feeling similar, there is almost 0 diversity in builds outside of weapon and skill choice. In the end your choice of skill is the only thing that really matters and will be how you deal all your damage. You will just get gear that buffs your weapon and skill of choice and that's it you have your build. There are some cool progression mechanics and that is the main thing this game does well, you are always moving some sort of number up. Outside of the progression mechanics the game feels very janky, skills dont interact with each other or have skill trees for any sort of player expression, and as a whole it just left me feeling kinda dirty, and wondering why I wasnt playing any of the other ARPGs I own. I imagine thats the main type of person who will enjoy this game, someone that has already played PoE, played Last Epoch, Grim Dawn, hell I would even recommend playing Heroes Siege or Torchlight Infinite over this. But if your a degenerate like me and have played all of those games to hell then you may get some brief enjoyment from this game, and the pricetag is low. if your one of those people, go buy Siralim Ultimate right now and play that, theres no way you have played that one too right? Well if you have, then buy this at your own risk. The numbers do be going up tho.

[h1]This may be one of the saddest games I have ever played. [/h1] [b]In short: This is a very low effort and boring, uninspired combination of the worst parts of two good genres. [/b] [b]Nothing[/b] about this is good. It is a walking walking simulator that kills enemies around you. This feels, plays, and looks just like a mobile game. The only potential upside compared to a mobile game is that you pay up front; instead of micro-transaction pay-to-win, some sort of gacha system, or loads of ads. Progression feels pointless, difficulty is nonexistent, and every boss, including the big ones that are the entirety of a level, are just damage sponges with [b]THREE[/b] (3) attacks. That is not hyperbole; they only have three. It is the worst type of endless time sink grind I may have ever seen. There are countless better games that are better designed, more appealing, and most importantly more fun. [b]Every[/b] asset is clearly from an asset store. Let me be clear in that buying and using assets is not bad or wrong, but literally [b]EVERYTHING[/b] is a bought asset, in an already terribly designed and boring game. This is an asset flip. The only original work done is POSSIBLY the programming and some of the system designs; as boring and low effort as they are. As a solo developer, this is one to four months (four being pretty generous) worth of work if you were also working a full time job. Implementing all the assets was likely the largest portion of the work done. I have no clue how this got out of early access, much less onto the steam store. I also have no clue where all these positive reviews are coming from, because everything is just so awful. I have a strong feeling they are fake and/or botted. [u]Also zero dwarfs. Literally zero.[/u]

What a weird game. It's not really bad, it's just extremely mediocre. I got it for 5€, but I don't know if I'd recommend this unless you're extremely pressed on gaming time and can handle some massive jank when playing. At it's core, it's an very simple WASD-movement survivors-like. People keep saying it's an "ARPG", but nah, it's a somewhat watered down asset flip survivorslike from a 3rd person view. Slapping a rarity loot system and a monkey version of PoE's skilltree on top of a survivorslike game doesn't make it an ARPG. The thing that baffles me with it is that where the gameplay is super simple (kill enemies, press E to loot stuff), the entire game is made massively confusing by the extremely awful UI design. You enter a level on a highly unreadable map, kill enemies and the boss, loot some stuff, return to your town, and are then greeted with 5-6 different work stations which all require you to wait through a short animation to do whatever said work station does. While the functionality of the stations is simple (forge crafts ignots by pressing one button etc.), the bad UI design makes all this quite annoying. For example, why would I ever want to go through each item in a workshop separately, crafting them by pressing C, when there's a "craft all" button on the extreme top left of the window? Why is this craft all button not the one bound to C? Why does the disenchantment table say "DISENCHANT ALL" below the buttons that select which items you want to disenchant, and then only disenchant the items you've selected for disenchantment? You also can NOT craft base gear to actually try and create your own gear. The workshop for equipment is only for adding stat affixes. I started building my talent tree for fist weapon damage, but I only got bows as drops, so time to respec, I guess. I still haven't gotten a single fist weapon in 2 hours of gameplay time. Gear is color coded for rarity, but said rarity is not specified in text in any part of the item description. I unlocked some workstation to modify "legendary" gear, which I would presume is orange, but didn't have any yet. I tried putting in some other gear, and the station gave me no feedback on what the issue with the gear piece was. Lack of information is blatant -- you have skills, and they apparently have affinities, but these are not stated ANYWHERE. It's minor stuff like this that really makes this feel like a rushed "my first game" type of deal. If you look at the leaderboards, everyone and their mom are running the same exact build with the same exact skills and items. It just speaks volumes about the balance and makes every other skill seem worthless in comparison. Speaking of skills, most of them seem underwhelming, at least in the Archery tree. The visual effects are boring, and while the skill tree has a SINGLE node for each skill to make them more viable, they're still left very underwhelming. I had to specifically stop doing any other damage and press R to activate an archer skill to see if it actually did anything other than a shooting animation because I could not see any visual effects for it (it was a small purple mist on the ground with a very small AOE). The talent tree is huge, but it is the wrong type of huge. Each point is basically "+1 damage", "+1 armor", or, if you're within a specified talent node section, "+1 archery damage", "+1 archery critical damage". The only times you get something interesting are the larger nodes, which instead give you "+10 archery damage", or perhaps modify a skill just a bit. Search for "archery" nodes, and you can only find that one single specific node group on the left side of the tree. No theorycrafting, only "+damage". It's so boring, you just need to find the specific node section for your weapon type, and build towards that. You can also level up single stats on level up in your character panel, but it feels pointless when the whatever fate card system can give you +15 of one in a single card, while a level up gives you +1. Also why does Stamina give you more health, and Endurance give you more energy? Why not the other way around? Makes no sense to me. Enemy hitboxes are ALL OVER THE PLACE. In a game like this, where everything always happens on a flat plane, this wouldn't be such an issue, but they *added verticality to combat for some insane reason*. Massive bosses can only be hit on their toes, so when your skill always flies up in a 45 degree angle, you will never hit them since your projectiles just fly through them. There are also mounts? Wtf? Why? It feels like bloat, and only added in because there was an asset in the Unity store to make it in a single day. The most confusing thing is that it's called "Dwarven Realms", and because I made a human character, I've yet to see a SINGLE dwarf character during my entire 2.4 hours of gameplay. So to sum it all up: * Horrible UI design makes the game confusing * Skills are bland and the VFX for them is nonexistent * Talent tree is awful and boring * Workshops waste time with short animations that stack up when done many times over a gameplay session * Gameplay loop is fast and can cause the "one more run" syndrome, but combat is muddled down by bad balance issues (everyone runs the same build for a reason) * No dwarves in "Dwarven Realms", unless you make your character a dwarf * Blatantly horrible hitboxes and combat verticality in a game where it is not needed. All of these issues would be fixable, but looking at the age of this game and the way it's focused on a content treadmill, I don't think they will ever be fixed. Buy only if you're highly starved for a survivorslike game.
